cards.method: Real-time data-revision analysis (vintages: a triangle, revision statistics, news-vs-noise/efficiency tests, a state-space nowcast)
cards.when: successive releases/vintages of the SAME macro series (real-time data) -> a revision triangle, revision summary statistics, news-vs-noise/bias/efficiency tests, or a state-space efficient final-estimate nowcast
cards.when_not: a single release (no vintage dimension); business-cycle dating (#88); plain forecast evaluation without vintages (#74-77); data ingestion (a file upload — a frontend route, not a node)

alternatives.criterion: you want a simple overview/heatmap of the revision table (wide: reference periods x publication dates)
you want the VALUES of the revisions relative to one reference; nth_release='latest' => the total revision (to the final release)
you want statistics + tests: bias/MAR/noise-to-signal/correlation/Theil and news-vs-noise (Mankiw-Shapiro)
you want to find the first release that is unbiased & efficient (b0=0 & b1=1, HAC)
you want a state-space 'efficient' estimate of the final value (Jacobs-van Norden news/noise or Kishor-Koenig)

output_key_fields: triangle: a matrix of reference periods against vintages, plus n_obs_per_period, the number of observed values per period
revisions: a frame {pub_date, time, revision} plus a summary (mean/sd/MAR/min/max, n_revisions counting the observed ones, n_missing)

sign_convention (compute_revisions): a mode-dependent string that travels WITH the numbers — 'revision = final - release' when nth_release='latest', against 'revision = reference - vintage (older - newer)' for an interval, a small nth_release, or a reference date; the OPPOSITE polarity from the sign_convention of analyze_revisions, which is 'final - initial'
revision_summary: a data_frame with one row per release (Bias(mean), MAR, noise/signal, Correlation, Theil's U, the news/noise test coefficient + p)
first_efficient_release: e, 0-indexed and blank when there is none, plus a tests frame {release, F_stat, p_value, efficient}
nowcast: the states and params frames, loglik/aic/bic/convergence/converged, and the raw fit as a stub
interpretation_traps: TWO different sign conventions: compute_revisions revision = REFERENCE - VINTAGE (nth_release='latest' => final - initial; interval/a small nth_release => NEGATIVE values for an upward-trending series); analyze_revisions revision = final - initial

news/noise polarity: the News test = a regression of the revision on the INITIAL value; the Noise test = a regression on the FINAL value (the coefficient point estimates coincide with a plain lm; HAC changes ONLY the SE/p-value)
the get_revision_analysis columns depend on the degree (1=magnitude/bias, 2=correlation, 3=news/noise, 4=Theil/sign, 5=all 38)
first_efficient_release: e is 0-indexed, so 0 means the first release is already efficient; when there is none it comes back blank with a warning — a valid result, not an error
nowcast: e MUST be >0 AND e<n_releases; the MLE is deterministic (identical when seeded); a small sample -> boundary/degenerate parameters
the node handles ONE series: several id values are blocked by a gate; unobserved revisions do NOT inflate n, since n_revisions counts only the observed ones
diagnose WAS OMITTED (a console-printing helper); the same statistics are exposed machine-readably by analyze_revisions
sources: Mankiw-Shapiro 1986 'News or Noise? An Analysis of GNP Revisions' Survey of Current Business (news vs noise)
Aruoba 2008 'Data Revisions Are Not Well Behaved' Journal of Money, Credit and Banking 40(2-3) 319-340 (the efficient release / Mincer-Zarnowitz test)
Jacobs & van Norden 2011 'Modeling data revisions: Measurement error and dynamics of true values' Journal of Econometrics 161(1) 101-109 (the jvn nowcast)
Kishor & Koenig 2012 'VAR Estimation and Forecasting When Data Are Subject to Revision' Journal of Business & Economic Statistics 30(2) 181-190 (the kk nowcast)

cards.method: Pseudo-real-time vintage construction from publication lags
cards.when: an honest out-of-sample exercise needs the data as they were, and a full vintage archive is rarely available
cards.when_not: a true vintage archive exists and should be used instead; the publication calendar is unknown

alternatives.criterion: acceptable only for series that are never revised

output_key_fields: vintages: the constructed data as of each date
ragged_edge: the availability pattern at each vintage
publication_lags: the lags applied per series
coverage: how much of each vintage is real rather than assumed
interpretation_traps: PSEUDO-REAL-TIME CAPTURES THE RAGGED EDGE BUT NOT REVISIONS: it reproduces what was available, not what the values then were, and for heavily revised series that is the larger error
publication lags change over time and across statistical agencies; a constant lag is an approximation that biases early vintages
using final data in a forecast evaluation overstates accuracy, sometimes dramatically for real-activity series

cards.when: which vintage counts as the truth changes the measured accuracy, and the choice must be stated rather than defaulted
cards.when_not: the series is never revised, where the question does not arise

alternatives.criterion: a compromise, released a stated number of periods later

output_key_fields: metrics: accuracy under each actual convention
convention: which vintage was treated as truth
revision_contribution: how much of the error is revision rather than forecast error
sensitivity: how the ranking of methods changes across conventions
interpretation_traps: THE RANKING OF FORECASTING METHODS CAN REVERSE between the first-release and final-vintage conventions; reporting one without the other is a choice that can determine the conclusion
forecasting the final value is a harder problem than forecasting the first release, and includes predicting the revision
revision noise is not forecast error, and separating them is the point of running both conventions

cards.when: seasonal adjustment revises past values as new data arrive, and the size of those revisions is a property of the adjustment, not of the economy
cards.when_not: the series is not seasonally adjusted; the archive is too short for sliding spans

alternatives.criterion: stability of the adjustment across overlapping samples
how much the adjusted values move as data arrive
the practical size of the problem

output_key_fields: sliding_spans: maximum percentage difference across spans
revision_history: revisions to adjusted values by vintage
unstable_periods: periods failing the stability threshold
concurrent_vs_final: the systematic gap
interpretation_traps: A SERIES CAN PASS EVERY IN-SAMPLE ADJUSTMENT DIAGNOSTIC AND STILL REVISE HEAVILY; sliding spans and revision history are the only checks that see this
the conventional sliding-span thresholds are rules of thumb from the Census Bureau, not statistical tests
forecast extension at the end of the sample is what drives most of the revision, so the last observations are always the least reliable
sources: Findley, Monsell, Shulman & Pugh 1990 (Journal of Business and Economic Statistics 8:1-16)
U.S. Census Bureau X-13ARIMA-SEATS Reference Manual

cards.when: reading vintage data from statistical services that publish revision history, so a real-time exercise uses real vintages
cards.when_not: no vintage archive is published for the series; the engine must not reach the network -- this routes through the external-data node

alternatives.criterion: the series has a real-time database
only the initial estimates are needed

output_key_fields: vintages: the retrieved vintage panel
vintage_dates: the dates available
source: which archive the data came from
coverage: series and periods actually returned
interpretation_traps: THIS NODE DOES NOT REACH THE NETWORK ITSELF: retrieval is delegated to the external-data node, and the engine's no-network property is preserved -- passing it a live endpoint is a contract violation
vintage dates are not release dates; a vintage labelled by month can contain data released at various points within it
archives differ in whether they store the full series at each vintage or only the changed observations
